newsitem.title: USA: Three teams picked to compete for warship.
newsitem.headline: Three teams picked to compete for warship.

text.p: The Pentagon on Friday picked three industry teams headed by Lockheed Martin Corp., Northrop Grumman Corp. and General Dynamics Corp. to compete in designing a new "Arsenal Ship" that could change naval warfare in five years.

The three teams, now narrowed from a field of five, each received a $15 million contract to work for one year on proposals for the missile-packed stealth warship. One team will be chosen next year to build a prototype of the vessel.
Final work on the proposed fleet of six ships could be worth more than $3 billion to the eventual winner. Tentative plans are to launch the first ship in the year 2001.

With military budgets and forces shrinking after the Cold War, the Pentagon has asked defence contractors to compete in designing a sleek and virtually unsinkable Navy ship packed with 500 missile launchers and space age communications.

Expected to cost $550 million each, a bargain at today's prices, each of the six ships would be manned by fewer than 50 sailors -- or perhaps no crew at all as they evolve -- with missiles and artillery that might even be triggered by Army officers ashore.

The new multi-hull weapons platform, which the Pentagon plans to develop aggressively and test in only five years compared to 15 normally needed for new ships, could patrol near world hotspots and maintain peace.
